title: Comfort that keeps you waiting

captions.energy: Leaving change in a suspended state
captions.emotions: Clinging to the comforts you know

meaning: Improving what is familiar can quietly secure an inconvenient routine when change is postponed to protect existing comfort.
text: Sometimes caring for home helps you adapt to something you have long wanted to change. The Empress in the physical position of Muladhara makes familiar life more pleasant: finding attractive covers, cooking favourites and adding useful details. The Hanged Man in energy tests your footing through a standstill that continues without reaching a decision. The Devil in emotions clings to familiar comfort even when it limits both people’s freedom. You do a great deal for home, yet each improvement allows you to avoid changing what troubles you a little longer.

Imagine a large television in a room with little space left for conversation or rest away from the screen. You choose a convenient cabinet, hide the cables and buy soft cushions. **Improving a habit is easier than acknowledging its cost.** The room becomes tidier, but each evening still revolves around one activity. Discussing another arrangement waits because the comfort you have gained feels hard to lose, while the free space exists only as an idea.

The vulnerability is treating further investment as proof that the old routine must stay. The more care it contains, the harder it becomes to question. The standstill starts to look like sensible thrift, although it prevents other uses of home. Support restores freedom when valuing your past effort does not oblige you to preserve indefinitely the form that once called for it.
